messages.content: You check each debater against its own earlier words. You bring nothing from outside the words given to you: no doctrine, no training knowledge, no reading of your own. You do not judge who is right, and you do not judge one side by the other side's words.

You are the closing enforcer. A debater's closing round may not contradict what the same debater stated in its earlier rounds. Below are one debater's four rounds.
Read its closing round against its earlier rounds. List every closing sentence that cannot be true together with an earlier sentence, and answer every candidate listed.
A contradiction is two statements that cannot both be true. Two sentences of the same closing round that cannot both be true are also a contradiction: quote the first as EARLIER [<round 4>] and the second as CLOSING [<round 4>]. A closing sentence that asserts again, as the debater's own, what it withdrew, dropped, narrowed or gave up in an earlier round IS a contradiction. A closing sentence that restores the wider wording or the ground of a claim the debater narrowed or gave up in an earlier round ("I narrow", "I withdraw", "I do not rest") asserts it again; check the close against every one listed under EARLIER NARROWINGS.
It is NOT a contradiction when the closing sentence: grants, concedes, narrows or withdraws something; states or quotes the other side's position; answers a press with a further reason the earlier sentence leaves room for; differs only in wording; or differs only by a reference: it ties its point to a verse whose words, as the debater's own rounds quote them, do not give that point (a wrong reference, or one grouped with the verse that does give it). Read such a sentence with that reference set aside; if its point then agrees with the earlier sentence, it is not a contradiction. A sentence whose point itself cannot be true with the earlier sentence is still a contradiction, whatever its references.
Read a withdrawal by its meaning, not its words: a closing sentence that says again in other words what the earlier sentence withdrew, dropped or gave up, or rests its reason on it, asserts it again. "Differs only in wording" clears two sentences that make the same claim; it never clears a closing sentence that makes again a claim the debater withdrew. A closing sentence that states only what the debater kept, or rests the same conclusion on other rows, does not assert it again. When the earlier sentence rests no weight on a verse or row, a closing sentence that uses that verse or row as a footing for the same link or the same purpose asserts it again.
Read each candidate's closing sentence together with the rows of its CLOSING BLOCK: a closing sentence that draws its point from a row ("So", "Therefore", "Thus") asserts what that row says, so if the earlier sentence withdrew, dropped or rested nothing on that row, the close asserts it again.
Quote both sentences word for word and name the link: the link whose closing block holds the sentence, else the link the earlier sentence supports.
Reply with one line per contradiction and per candidate, and nothing else:
CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: <candidate id or NEW> -- <DEFENDER|CHALLENGER> -- LINK <n> -- CONFIRMED | NOT A CONTRADICTION -- EARLIER [<round>] "<words>" -- CLOSING [<round 4>] "<words>" -- <one sentence: why both cannot be true, or why they can>
If you find none and there is no candidate, reply: CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NONE

CANDIDATES ALREADY NAMED (answer each one by its id):
none

EARLIER NARROWINGS (this side's own, rounds 1 to 3, listed by the code; the narrowing sentence is marked >> <<; check the close against each, and write NEW for a contradiction you find):
none

######## THE DEFENDER ########
The defender's links: D1 = LINK 1, D2 = LINK 2, D3 = LINK 3, D4 = LINK 4, D5 = LINK 5 (its DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1]). Its closing round is [CR4].

=== [CR1] ===
DEFENDER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

The question is answered by the rows that name the father, name the seed, and name the knowing.

The seed promised is out of a man's body. [L1] "And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom." 2 Samuel 7:12 [L2] zera (H2233) meaning seed, posterity [L3] "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." Psalm 132:11 [L4] The promise requires seed proceeding out of bowels and body, footed on the stating verse and the body row beside it.

That seed is said of Jesus according to the flesh. [L1] "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" Romans 1:3 [L2] sperma (G4690) meaning something sown, that is seed including the male sperm, by implication offspring [L3] "Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;" Acts 2:30 [L4] The flesh seed is out of loins, footed on the stating verse and the loins row beside it. [L1] "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood." Hebrews 7:14 [L2] osphys (G3751) meaning the loin externally, the hip, internally by extension procreative power, standing in "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." Hebrews 7:10 [L3] "Take ye the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of their names, every male by their polls;" Numbers 1:2 [L4] The springing out of Juda is evident in the fathers' reckoning, footed on the stating verse and the reckoning row.

The man the text names as father is Joseph. [L1] "And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:48 [L2] pater (G3962) meaning a father literally or figuratively, near or more remote [L3] "And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" John 6:42 [L4] The mother and the town name the same father, footed on the mother's speech and the town's speech beside it. [L1] "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20 with its margin "conceived: Gr. begotten" [L2] gennao (G1080) meaning to procreate properly of the father, but by extension of the mother [L3] "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary." Luke 1:27 [L4] The row that carries conceived names Joseph son of David and Mary thy wife in one mouth, footed on the stating verse and the house row.

The canon's stated means of such begetting is knowing. [L1] "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD." Genesis 4:1 [L2] yada (H3045) meaning to know [L3] "So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the LORD gave her conception, and she bare a son." Ruth 4:13 [L4] Knowing and going in unto stand where conception stands, footed on the stating verse and the Boaz row. [L1] "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Matthew 1:19 [L1] "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25 [L2] ginosko (G1097) meaning to know [L3] "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" Matthew 1:24 [L4] Husband and wife from the espousal, taking then withholding till the birth, place the begetting within the espousal before the withheld span, footed on the husband-wife rows and the took-till rows.

"Of the Holy Ghost" does not name another begetter. [L1] "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:18 [L2] ek (G1537) meaning of, from, origin [L3] "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." John 3:6 [L4] Of the Holy Ghost marks covenant origin and anointing, not flesh begetting, footed on the stating row read whole with Matthew 1:20 and the flesh-Spirit distinction. [L1] "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." Luke 1:35 [L2] eperchomai (G1904) meaning to come upon [L3] "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth." Acts 1:8 [L4] Come upon is power for witness, footed on the same word in the witness row. [L1] "While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud." Luke 9:34 [L2] episkiazo (G1982) meaning to overshadow, to cast a shade [L3] "While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him." Matthew 17:5 [L4] Overshadow is the presence cloud, footed on the cloud rows.

"Son of God" does not decide begetting. [L1] "I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men:" 2 Samuel 7:14 [L2] ben (H1121) meaning son [L3] "And he said unto me, Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father." 1 Chronicles 28:6 [L4] The covenant son has a named father of flesh beside God's covenant fatherhood, footed on the stating verse and the Solomon row. [L1] "I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee." Psalm 2:7 [L3] "God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee." Acts 13:33 [L4] The begetting of the title is applied at the raising up, footed on the psalm and its applied occasion.

DECLARED CHAIN
D1: The promised seed proceeds out of a man's bowels and loins -- exhibits 2 Samuel 7:12 [L1] with zera seed posterity [L2] and Psalm 132:11 [L3], inferring flesh seed out of the body [L4].
D2: Jesus is made of that seed of David according to the flesh, sprung out of Juda -- exhibits Romans 1:3 [L1] with sperma something sown including male sperm by implication offspring [L2] and Acts 2:30 with Hebrews 7:14 [L3], inferring a flesh seed in the fathers' line [L4].
D3: The father named in four mouths is Joseph son of David -- exhibits Luke 2:48 with John 6:42 [L1] with pater father literally [L2] and Luke 1:27 with Matthew 1:20 naming Joseph thou son of David with Mary thy wife [L3], inferring the named Davidic father [L4].
D4: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and of the Holy Ghost is covenant origin -- exhibits Genesis 4:1 with Matthew 1:19, Matthew 1:24, Matthew 1:25 [L1] with yada to know and ginosko to know [L2] and Ruth 4:13 with John 3:6 [L3], inferring the union before the withheld span and the Spirit as anointing [L4].
D5: Yes, Christ had a biological father, Joseph the named Davidic father -- exhibits Romans 1:3 with Acts 2:30 [L1] with sperma something sown including male sperm [L2] and Luke 2:48 with Matthew 1:20 [L3], inferring the seed honored through the named line [L4].

=== [CR2] ===
DEFENDER (record's reading) -- ROUND 2, RESPONSE

My chain stands. Each press below is re-seated in its chain, with the verses that state it.

**Answer to A1 -- the child before the coming together**

[L1] "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:18 [L3] "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" Matthew 1:24 [L4] The coming together Matthew 1:18 dates is answered by what Matthew narrates next as the taking, "took unto him his wife" in Matthew 1:24, the coming under one roof, footed on the finding row and the taking row together.

[L1] "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child." Luke 2:5 [L2] patēr (G3962) meaning a father literally or figuratively, near or more remote, standing in "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:48 [L3] "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Matthew 1:19 [L4] The rows name "Joseph her husband" in Matthew 1:19 and "Mary thy wife" in Matthew 1:20, and Mary names Joseph "thy father" in Luke 2:48, footed on the husband row and the father word together.

It fits the link D4: husband and wife from the espousal, the finding before the taking, the begetting within the espousal.

**Answer to A2 -- knew her not till**

[L1] "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25 [L3] "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" Matthew 1:24 [L3] "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD." Genesis 4:1 [L4] The not-knowing is told after the taking and bounded by till to the birth, covering the pregnancy after the taking, while the canon's stated means of conceiving is knowing, footed on the took-till order and the Adam-knew row.

[L1] "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20 with its margin "conceived: Gr. begotten" [L2] sperma (G4690) meaning something sown, that is seed including the male sperm, by implication offspring, standing in "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" Romans 1:3 [L3] "So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the LORD gave her conception, and she bare a son." Ruth 4:13 [L4] The row that carries conceived names the husband and wife in one mouth, and the LORD's hand at a conception stands with the husband going in, footed on the whole row and the Boaz row.

It fits the link: the withholding runs from the taking to the birth; the begetting stands before it.

**Answer to B1 -- for that which is conceived is of the Holy Ghost**

[L1] "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20 [L2] theos (G2316) meaning a deity, especially with the article the supreme Divinity, standing in the Holy Ghost phrase of this row [L3] "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." John 3:6 [L4] Of the Holy Ghost marks covenant origin and anointing, not flesh begetting, since flesh and Spirit are kept as two kinds, footed on the whole row naming Joseph son of David and the flesh-Spirit distinction.

[L1] "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Matthew 1:19 [L3] "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20 [L4] The for grounds the command to take her because the child is holy, the seed God claims, footed on the intent row and the angel's reason row.

It fits the link D3: the reason names the father of the house in the same breath it names the Spirit.

**Answer to B2 -- she shall bring forth, thou shalt call**

[L1] "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins." Matthew 1:21 [L2] huios (G5207) meaning a son, used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively kinship, standing in "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" Romans 1:3 [L3] "But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John." Luke 1:13 [L4] Joseph is given the father's naming charge as Zacharias was, installing him in the house as husband and namer, footed on the naming row and the Zacharias parallel.

It fits the link: naming is the father's act, not a guardian's substitute.

**Answer to C1 -- I know not a man**

[L1] "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:34 [L3] "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary." Luke 1:27 [L3] "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD." Genesis 4:1 [L4] Her words state her present state when spoken, espoused to Joseph, against the canon's stated means of knowing, footed on the espoused row and the Adam-knew row. Her speech in Luke 1:34 gives present knowing words, "I know not a man," in the present tense she speaks.

It fits the link D4: present state, not a denial of the union.

**Answer to C2 -- come upon, overshadow, therefore**

[L1] "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." Luke 1:35 [L2] For eperchomai the record gives the same construction standing in "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth." Acts 1:8 [L3] "While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud." Luke 9:34 [L4] Come upon is power for witness in Acts 1:8, and overshadow is the presence cloud in Luke 9:34, each carrying empowerment and presence, footed on the same-word rows.

[L1] "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:" Luke 1:32 [L2] thronos (G2362) meaning a stately seat throne, by implication power, standing in "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;" Acts 2:30 [L3] "And he said unto me, Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father." 1 Chronicles 28:6 [L4] The title and the throne of his father David are given before she asks how, rooted in the covenant as Solomon's sonship was, footed on the throne-given row and the Solomon row.

It fits the link: the therefore connects back to the throne covenant, not to a begetting by the Spirit.

**Answer to C3 -- declared by the resurrection**

[L1] "And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:" Romans 1:4 [L3] "God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee." Acts 13:33 [L3] "I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee." Psalm 2:7 [L4] The begetting of the title is applied at the raising up, footed on the declared row and its psalm occasion.

It fits the link: Son of God is covenant and resurrection title, deciding no flesh begetter.

**Answer to D1 -- the virgin sign**

[L1] "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." Isaiah 7:14 [L3] "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying," Matthew 1:22 [L3] "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." Matthew 1:23 [L4] Matthew ties all this, Matthew 1:18-21 read whole with Joseph husband, Mary wife, and Joseph naming, to the sign, footed on the sign row and the fulfilled rows.

It fits the link: the sign is fulfilled in the account that names the father, not against it.

**Answer to E1 -- Matthew 1:16 passive**

[L1] "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." Matthew 1:16 [L3] "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren;" Matthew 1:2 [L3] "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" Romans 1:3 [L4] The genealogy row names Joseph the husband of Mary with Jesus born of her, and the seed according to the flesh is stated in Romans 1:3 and in Acts 2:30 of the fruit of loins, footed on the genealogy row and the seed rows together.

It fits the link D5: the chain fills what the one verse leaves quiet.

**Answer to F1 -- thy father, my Father's business**

[L1] "And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:48 [L2] patēr (G3962) meaning a father literally or figuratively, near or more remote [L3] "And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Luke 2:49 [L4] Mary names Joseph father of flesh in direct speech, and his answer names the covenant Father above, two fatherhoods in one exchange, footed on the mother's speech and the answer beside it.

[L1] "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:" Luke 1:32 [L3] "I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men:" 2 Samuel 7:14 [L4] David called his father and God his father stand together as covenant title beside flesh lineage, footed on the throne row and the covenant formula.

It fits the link D3: the gloss admits figurative, the context fixes Joseph as the near father.

**Answer to F2 -- whose father and mother we know, as was supposed**

[L1] "And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" John 6:42 [L3] "And all bare him witness, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth. And they said, Is not this Joseph's son?" Luke 4:22 [L4] The town states knowledge of father and mother in plain words, footed on the town's speech and its second witness.

[L1] "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli," Luke 3:23 [L3] "And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:48 [L4] The supposing stands with Mary's thy father, decided by context for the named father, footed on the genealogy row and the mother's row.

It fits the link: the town confirms what Mary said.

**Answer to G1-G3 -- seed, made, sprang, house**

[L1] "And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom." 2 Samuel 7:12 [L2] zera (H2233) meaning seed, figuratively fruit, plant, sowing-time, posterity [L3] "And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel." Genesis 3:15 [L4] Her seed names the woman's offspring with the father given in the begetting chain, as Seth called seed has Adam knowing Eve in Genesis 4:1, footed on the bowels row and the woman-seed row read with its begetting chain.

[L1] "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" Romans 1:3 [L2] sperma (G4690) meaning something sown, that is seed including the male sperm, by implication offspring [L3] "Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;" Acts 2:30 [L4] Made of seed according to the flesh with fruit of loins according to the flesh requires seed out of a man's body, footed on the made row and the loins row.

[L1] "For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham." Hebrews 2:16 with its margin "Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold" [L3] "Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;" Hebrews 2:14 [L4] He takes hold of Abraham's seed likewise as the children, in the same flesh and blood, footed on the taketh-hold row with its margin and the likewise row.

[L1] "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood." Hebrews 7:14 [L2] osphys (G3751) meaning the loin externally, that is the hip, internally by extension procreative power, standing in "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." Hebrews 7:10 [L3] "Take ye the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of their names, every male by their polls;" Numbers 1:2 [L4] The evident springing out of Juda is shown in loins of the father and reckoned by the house of the fathers, footed on the evident row with the loin word and the reckoning row.

[L1] "And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:)" Luke 2:4 [L3] "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" Romans 1:3 [L4] House and lineage name the register; seed according to the flesh names the body; the body rows carry the seed out of loins, footed on the house row and the seed row.

It fits the links D1, D2, D5: the seed rows require a man's loins and bowels, honored through Joseph, the son of David Mary calls father.

=== [CR3] ===
DEFENDER (record's reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

LINK 4 [premise 1]: SUPPORTED -- the begetting stands inside the espousal, before the finding, with Joseph named husband in the same account.
[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L2] aner (G435) "a man (properly as an individual male):--fellow, husband, man, sir" stands in Matthew 1:19 in "Joseph her husband."
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]" -- the same account names her "Mary thy wife."
[L1] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD. [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]"
[L3] Ruth 4:13: "So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the LORD gave her conception, and she bare a son."
[L4] It fits the link D4: husband and wife from the espousal are named in Matthew 1:19-20, and the canon's stated means of begetting is knowing / going in unto, with the LORD's hand named beside the husband in the same row or chain, so the begetting within the espousal rests on those rows. Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." dates the finding; Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" is the coming under one roof, answered by Matthew 1:24 with Matthew 1:18. Luke 2:5: "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child. [taxed: or, enrolled]" keeps the espoused name with the pregnancy.

LINK 4 [premise 2]: SUPPORTED -- "of the Holy Ghost" marks covenant origin and anointing, not flesh begetting.
